1	# Production deployment
2	
3	How to stand DataQ up in production. This is the operator's overview; the exhaustive
4	provisioning runbook, the OpenTofu stack, and the complete env-var reference live in
5	[`deploy/README.md`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/deploy/README.md) and
6	[`deploy/terraform/azure/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/azure).
7	Azure is the supported target today; AWS/GCP are planned behind the same seams.
8	
9	## Topology
10	
11	```
12	Browser ──HTTPS──► Frontend Container App (nginx + SPA — the ONLY public ingress)
13	AI clients ─MCP──► │  proxies /api + /mcp + /healthz same-origin
14	                   ▼
15	              FastAPI (internal ingress) ──► PostgreSQL
16	                   │  ├──► Celery worker ──► GX execution ──► your datasources
17	                   │  ├──► Redis (task queue)
18	                   │  ├──► Key Vault (secrets)
19	                   │  └──► App Insights / OTLP (observability)
20	```
21	
22	The frontend is the sole public surface; the API is internal and reached only through the
23	frontend proxy (ADR 0028 §5).
24	
25	## Prerequisites
26	
27	- A **container platform** — Azure Container Apps in the reference deploy (API + worker +
28	  frontend apps, a one-shot migrate **job**, and Redis).
29	- **PostgreSQL** (a dedicated database + a least-privilege app role).
30	- A **secret store** — Azure Key Vault, reached via a managed identity.
31	- An **OIDC identity provider** — app registrations for the API (audience) and the SPA.
32	- **Observability** — Application Insights and/or a generic OTLP endpoint.
33	- A container registry the platform can pull from (GHCR in the reference).
34	
35	## 1. Provision
36	
37	Use the in-repo OpenTofu stack ([`deploy/terraform/azure/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/azure),
38	ADR 0024) to stand up the app stack — the Container Apps, the migrate job, Redis, Key Vault +
39	managed identity, App Insights, and the SSO app registrations — plus a dedicated database and
40	least-priv role on your Postgres server. Set the required **GitHub environment variables and
41	Key Vault secrets** (full list in the deploy README) — never ship the eval/dev defaults.
42	
43	## 2. Deploy
44	
45	Deployment is a **manual GitHub Actions workflow** (`workflow_dispatch` → **Deploy**). Each
46	run, in order:
47	
48	1. **Builds + pushes** the backend and frontend images (tag defaults to the immutable commit
49	   SHA).
50	2. **Runs migrations** — a Container Apps job runs `alembic upgrade head` and the workflow
51	   **waits for it to succeed** *before* rolling anything. Migrations are additive/
52	   backward-compatible, so the still-running old code tolerates the new schema.
53	3. **Rolls** the API + worker, then the frontend (gated on the backend succeeding — no partial
54	   deploys).
55	
56	Use an immutable image tag per release; push-on-merge is intentionally off.
57	
58	## 3. Verify
59	
60	Run the **pre-deploy** and **post-deploy smoke** checklists in
61	[`deploy/README.md`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/deploy/README.md#pre-deploy-checklist)
62	around every deploy. In short:
63	
64	- **Before:** CI green on the SHA, docs up to date, migrations safe, secrets/config in place.
65	- **After:** `/healthz` → 200; a user can **sign in**; the **UI renders** (key pages, desktop
66	  + mobile); **every high-level flow works** end-to-end; auth is enforced (`401` on the API
67	  and MCP — MCP must be `401`, **not** `421`); prod docs are gated (`404`); and the api /
68	  worker / frontend are on the deployed tag with the migrate job `Succeeded`.
69	
70	## Running DataQ without Azure
71	
72	Azure is **one implementation behind each seam, never the architecture** (ADR
73	[0010](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md)).
74	Every seam has a working non-Azure implementation, so a fresh clone runs the
75	whole product — API, worker, scheduler, UI, checks — with **zero Azure
76	configuration** (#591):
77	
78	| Seam | Azure implementation | Local / non-Azure implementation |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| Secrets | Key Vault (`SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`) | `SECRET_STORE=openbao` — OpenBao in compose (the default in `.env.app.example`), or `env` for host-only dev. ADR [0039](adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md); the store speaks the KV v2 API, so the same mode also serves Vault or HCP |
81	| Auth | Entra SSO (`AZURE_*`) | **Email OTP** for humans (`AUTH_EMAIL_*` + an allowlist — ADR [0032](adr/0032-email-otp-signin.md)); `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true` for local dev; **PATs** (`dq_live_…`) for headless REST/MCP — see [API keys](api-keys.md). `/mcp` is served in every one of these modes; under OTP it accepts **PATs only** (no IdP ⇒ no bearer token to validate) |
82	| Observability | App Insights connection string | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` → any OTLP consumer; `docker-compose --profile telemetry up` starts a local Jaeger (UI on `:16686`). Unset ⇒ telemetry off, which is a supported posture, not a degraded one |
83	| Queue / cache | — | Redis in compose (same image as prod) |
84	| Database | Shared Azure Postgres | Postgres in compose |
85	| Lineage catalog | — | `docker-compose --profile lineage up` starts Marquez (dev-only reference consumer, ADR 0034) |
86	
87	```bash
88	git clone <repo> && cd DataQ
89	./scripts/setup.sh          # conda env, hooks, images, migrations, seed data
90	docker-compose up           # postgres + redis + openbao + api + worker + frontend
91	```
92	
93	`.env.app.example` ships with the local-first values already selected
94	(`SECRET_STORE=openbao`, `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, both telemetry endpoints blank);
95	every `AZURE_*` key may stay empty. Nothing in the app reads an Azure SDK unless
96	the corresponding seam is explicitly pointed at Azure.
97	
98	**What is not available locally** is *datasources*, not the platform: a
99	Snowflake or ADLS **connection** needs a live Snowflake or ADLS to run against.
100	The local-first path keeps flat files (local + S3), Unity Catalog (Databricks
101	Free Edition), and Iceberg. The test suite is unaffected either way — its
102	datasource reads are stubbed, so `pytest` is green with no cloud credentials of
103	any kind.
104	
105	## Operating notes
106	
107	- **Backward-compatible migrations only** — no `DROP`/rename/`NOT NULL`-without-default in the
108	  same release as the code that needs it. An `ALTER` on a hot table can briefly block on a
109	  live-worker lock; recovery + hardening are documented in the deploy README.
110	- **Secrets rotate** without a redeploy (they're read from the store at runtime); restart the
111	  dependent apps after a shared-Postgres recreate (start-time secret snapshot).
112	- The reference deployment carries **demo/test fixtures** — tear them down before any
113	  customer-facing or marketplace use (see the deploy README's operational notes).
114

116	the checklists — see

## AWS reference deployment

The same product deploys to AWS from the in-repo OpenTofu stack
([`deploy/terraform/aws/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/aws)) —
identical images, identical topology, each seam pointed at the AWS implementation:

```
Browser ──HTTPS──► CloudFront (public surface, origin secret verified at nginx)
                   ▼
              ALB ──► frontend (ECS Fargate, nginx + SPA) ──proxies──► api (ECS Fargate)
                   │  api/worker sidecars: ADOT collector → X-Ray traces + CloudWatch logs
                   ├──► RDS PostgreSQL          ├──► ElastiCache Redis (TLS)
                   ├──► AWS Secrets Manager     └──► SES (email alerts)
              Cognito (OIDC issuer for the SPA + API)
```

- **Secrets:** `SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager` (fourth store behind the seam).
- **Auth:** Amazon Cognito through the same generic OIDC contract (`DATAQ_AUTH_*`,
  `AUTH_OIDC_*`) — the second issuer validated in a real deployment after Azure AD. Cognito
  needs `DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE=cognito` (its `/logout` is not RP-Initiated-Logout
  conformant) and resolves the user profile via the **userinfo endpoint** (its access tokens
  carry neither `email` nor `aud`).
- **Observability:** the app's vendor-neutral OTLP export feeds an **ADOT collector sidecar**
  → X-Ray traces + OpenTelemetry logs in CloudWatch with matching trace ids.
- **Deploy:** a parallel **Deploy (AWS)** workflow (`deploy-aws.yml`) — GitHub OIDC role
  login, immutable `aws-<sha>` tags, migrate run-task gated on exit 0, then ECS service
  rolls and a CloudFront smoke.
- **Gotchas** (full list in the
  [AWS README](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/deploy/terraform/aws/README.md)):
  a `rediss://` broker URL needs `ssl_cert_reqs` (the app now defaults it to `required`);
  task definitions are under `ignore_changes`, so env/sidecar edits need a targeted
  `tofu apply -replace`; CloudFront sends an **origin secret header** that nginx enforces,
  so a third-party distribution cannot origin-point at the ALB.

All done. Here's the full picture:

## Repo status
The last AWS deploy (on `9e21d596`) was indeed cancelled mid-run: the backend job succeeded, the frontend job was cancelled. Investigating the AWS side turned up something worse than a stale image — **the #1378 origin-secret frontend image had never booted at all**. The 40-char CloudFront origin secret makes the nginx guard's static map key 81 bytes, over nginx's 64-byte `map_hash_bucket_size` default, so every new task exited at startup (`EssentialContainerExited` crash loop) while the old revision kept serving — meaning #1355 enforcement had silently never taken effect. The PR's local proof passed because its test secret was shorter than production's. Filed [#1380](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1380), fixed in [#1381](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1381) (with a second live-found gotcha: the directive must precede the *first* `map` block or nginx rejects it as duplicate), verified against a real nginx with a real-length secret — full guard matrix 403/403/200/200 on, 200/200 off.

## Docs (including GitHub Pages) — updated and published
- **[deployment.md](docs/deployment.md)** — no longer says AWS is "planned": new AWS reference deployment section (topology, Cognito via the generic OIDC contract, `aws_secrets_manager`, ADOT→X-Ray, the Deploy (AWS) workflow, gotchas); the seam table gained the AWS implementations.
- **[changelog.md](docs/changelog.md)** — "AWS as a second deployment target" entry; **[security.md](docs/security.md)** and **[observability.md](docs/observability.md)** now cover both reference deployments.
- **[progress.md](docs/progress.md)** — snapshot recounted 51/40 → **48/37** after the close-out trio (#1355→#1378, #1363→#1376, #1338→#1377), plus the #1380/#1381 record; **CLAUDE.md §13** headline updated.
- Merged as [#1379](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1379) and [#1382](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1382); the Pages build published green and I verified the **live site** now serves the AWS content.

## Deployed to both clouds on `5ebb508d` — both green, both smoked
- **Azure** ([run 31925968368](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31925968368)): build → migrate → roll all green. Public-surface smoke: `/healthz` 200, SPA + deep-links 200, `/api` and `/mcp` both 401, `/docs` serves the SPA shell. (Local `az` session has expired, so the smoke ran against the public FQDN; an authenticated `/me` check will need you to `az login` again.)
- **AWS** ([run 31925969360](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31925969360)): all three services stable on the new task defs — the frontend crash loop is gone. CloudFront smoke 200/200/401/401; worker healthy (beat heartbeats green, ADOT sidecar running). Terraform plan showed **zero drift** beforehand — #1378's infra half was already applied, only the bootable image was missing.
- **#1355 enforcement is now real and validated**: ELB health checks pass via the exempt `/_alb-health` path, CloudFront-stamped requests are admitted, and direct-to-ALB access from outside is denied at the security group (CloudFront prefix list) with the nginx 403 as the second layer. The validation evidence #1378 had promised is now [posted on #1355](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1355).

Both code reviews came back clean, all branches are pruned, main is at `b1edf849`, and nothing AWS-side remains open.
So, what is now the parity among Azure, AWS & Local DataQ installation in terms of Hosting, Features and Harness

Here's the parity picture as of today (`b1edf849`, both clouds on `5ebb508d`):

## Hosting — full parity, different implementations behind the same seams

| Concern | Azure (primary prod) | AWS (second reference) | Local |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compute | Container Apps (api / worker / frontend + migrate job) | ECS Fargate (same three + migrate RunTask) | docker-compose |
| Public surface | Frontend ACA app (nginx, sole ingress; api internal) | CloudFront → ALB → frontend nginx (origin secret + SG prefix-list deny) | localhost |
| Database | Shared Azure PG (`dataq` DB, least-priv role) | RDS PostgreSQL | Postgres container |
| Queue | Redis container app (password) | ElastiCache (TLS, `ssl_cert_reqs` now app-defaulted) | Redis container |
| Secrets | Key Vault (managed identity) | Secrets Manager (task IAM role) | OpenBao (compose default) |
| Auth | Entra ID via generic OIDC | Cognito via the same generic OIDC contract | Email OTP (Mailpit) by default; dev-bypass opt-in |
| Observability | App Insights (OTel) | ADOT sidecar → X-Ray + CloudWatch | Off by default; Jaeger via `--profile telemetry` |
| IaC + deploy | `deploy/terraform/azure/` + `deploy.yml` | `deploy/terraform/aws/` + `deploy-aws.yml` (zero drift as of today) | `scripts/setup.sh` |

The images are byte-identical across all three — everything above is runtime config, which is the ADR 0010/0028 design working as intended.

## Features — effectively identical, with three genuine asymmetries

The application feature set (suites/checks, all five datasources, monitor kinds, assets/lineage, alerting, scheduling, MCP's 8 tools, PATs, rate limiting, PDF export) is the same code everywhere, and both clouds have now live-verified the load-bearing paths: Snowflake + UC + S3 suite runs, MCP E2E, and a real sign-in on each IdP. Real asymmetries:

1. **Alert email**: verified live on AWS (SES, sandbox-only — production access still needs the AWS support form). Azure prod alerts via Teams/Slack; email is configured-not-exercised there. Local can point at Mailpit.
2. **Orchestration providers**: ADF is inherently Azure-only; Airflow/dbt are provider-neutral but nothing on AWS *sends* those events yet (see harness below). The webhook receivers themselves are live on both clouds.
3. **Small open edges**: `RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS=3` is unconfirmed against a live AWS XFF (CloudFront adds a hop Azure doesn't), and #1274 (Iceberg over S3-compatible storage via pyarrow) is an any-deployment issue, not cloud-specific.

## Harness — this is where parity does *not* exist

- **Azure**: the full ADR 0021 harness (separate repo) — ADF pipelines, Airflow, dbt-lineage job, mockdata flows A–D — stopped-by-default with `harness_window.sh` to open test windows.
- **Local**: a validated Azure-free mirror — local Airflow + MinIO landing zone + fakesnow stand-in, prod-mirrored connections/suites via OpenBao (`LOCAL_MIRROR_RUNBOOK.md`). All flows green including a live Snowflake load.
- **AWS: none.** Its E2E was exercised directly (real Snowflake/UC/S3 through the app), but no orchestration source exists there — so trigger-on-pipeline-success, pipeline-run ingest, and poll fallback have never fired *on AWS*, and there's no equivalent of a test window. That's the one real capability gap: the code is deployed and identical, but unexercised for the orchestration slice.

Short version: **hosting and features are at parity (same product, three complete seam implementations, both clouds deployed and smoked on the same commit); the harness is Azure + local only, which leaves AWS's orchestration path deployed-but-never-fired.** If you want to close that, the cheapest route is pointing the local harness's Airflow callbacks at the AWS CloudFront URL for one window — no AWS-side infra needed.

# Deployment parity — Azure · AWS · Local

How the three reference installations compare, as of 2026-08-16 (both clouds deployed from
the same commit). The design intent (ADR
[0010](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) /
[0028](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/adr/0028-cloud-neutral-frontend-and-auth.md))
is that **every difference lives in deploy-time configuration — there are zero
cloud-conditional code paths**, and the same container images run everywhere.

## Hosting

| Concern | Azure (primary reference) | AWS (second reference) | Local (compose) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compute | Container Apps: api / worker / frontend + migrate **job** | ECS Fargate: same three services + migrate **run-task** | docker-compose services |
| Public surface | Frontend Container App (sole public ingress; api internal-only) | CloudFront → ALB → frontend (the ALB security group admits only the CloudFront managed prefix list; nginx re-verifies an origin-secret header) | `localhost` |
| Images | One generic GHCR image set, tag `<sha>` | Same images, tag `aws-<sha>` | Same images |
| Database | PostgreSQL (dedicated database + least-privilege app role) | RDS PostgreSQL | Postgres container |
| Queue / cache | Redis (password auth) | ElastiCache Redis (TLS `rediss://`) | Redis container |
| Secret store | Key Vault (`SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`, managed identity) | Secrets Manager (`SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager`, task IAM role) | OpenBao (`openbao`), or `env` for host-only dev |
| Identity — humans | Entra ID through the generic OIDC contract | Cognito through the same contract | Email OTP (bundled Mailpit) by default; dev-bypass opt-in |
| Identity — machines | PATs (`dq_live_`) — identical everywhere | ← same | ← same |
| Observability | App Insights via OTel | ADOT collector sidecar → X-Ray + CloudWatch | Off by default; Jaeger via `--profile telemetry` |
| Email transport | Any SMTP relay | SES (note: a sandboxed SES account can only mail verified addresses) | Mailpit catcher |
| IaC | [`deploy/terraform/azure/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/azure) | [`deploy/terraform/aws/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/deploy/terraform/aws) | `scripts/setup.sh` + compose |

## Features

The application feature set — suites/checks across all five datasources, every monitor kind,
assets/lineage/incidents, alerting, scheduling, the 8-tool MCP server, PATs, rate limiting —
is the **same code everywhere**. Where the installations genuinely differ:

| Capability | Azure | AWS | Local |
|---|---|---|---|
| Datasource runs | live-verified: Snowflake, Unity Catalog, ADLS, S3/S3-compatible, Iceberg | live-verified: Snowflake, Unity Catalog, native S3 | flat files, MinIO, Unity Catalog (Free Edition), Iceberg; no live warehouse required |
| Alerting — Teams / Slack | live-verified | deployed, unexercised | pointable anywhere |
| Alerting — email | configured | live-verified (SES) | Mailpit |
| MCP (8 tools) | E2E-verified | E2E-verified (PAT) | works; PAT-only under OTP (no IdP ⇒ no bearer) |
| Rate limiting | on (`RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS=3`, verified against a live XFF) | on (same setting; not yet confirmed against a live CloudFront-chain XFF) | off by design |
| Orchestration — ADF | ✅ (Azure-only by nature) | n/a | n/a |
| Orchestration — Airflow / dbt | live-verified | **deployed but never fired** — the receivers are live, but no event source exists on that stack | local Airflow |

The Airflow/dbt row is the one real capability gap: the code is identical and deployed, but
the orchestration slice has never been exercised against the AWS installation. The cheapest
closure is pointing an external Airflow's callbacks at the AWS public URL.

## Test harness

| | Azure | AWS | Local |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mock-data / flow harness | Full external harness (ADF pipelines, Airflow, dbt job; opened on demand) | **none** | Self-contained mirror: local Airflow + MinIO landing zone + an open-source Snowflake stand-in |
| Orchestration event source | ADF + Airflow + dbt | none | local Airflow |

## Deploying: Azure vs AWS

Both deploy workflows are `workflow_dispatch`-only with the same shape — backend job first
(build → **migrate, gated on success** → roll api + worker), then the frontend job gated on
the backend; a blank `image_tag` input defaults to the immutable commit SHA. The real
differences:

| | Azure `deploy.yml` | AWS `deploy-aws.yml` |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud login | Azure OIDC federated credential | AWS OIDC role, trusting `repo:…:environment:production` |
| Tag namespace | `<sha>` | `aws-<sha>` (parallel deploys from one registry never collide) |
| Migrations | Container Apps job start + poll until `Succeeded` | Register a migrate task-def revision + `run-task` with the api service's live network config, gated on container exit 0 |
| Roll + verify | `az containerapp update` per app + revision verify | Shared `scripts/ci/ecs_roll.sh`: register → `update-service` → `wait services-stable` → verify the **primary deployment's image**, so an ECS circuit-breaker rollback fails the run instead of reporting success |
| In-workflow smoke | none (the deploy README checklists are run manually) | final public-surface smoke against the `AWS_FRONTEND_URL` repo variable |
| Sidecars | n/a | the roll script swaps/verifies the *essential* container (api/worker task defs also carry the ADOT sidecar) |
| Rollout gotcha | — | task definitions are under `ignore_changes[container_definitions]`: env/sidecar changes need a targeted `tofu apply -replace` + `update-service`; the workflow only ever moves the image |

## Configuration: what actually differs

Most backend env is **identical in shape on both clouds** (`ENVIRONMENT`, `DATABASE_URL`,
`REDIS_URL`, `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false`, `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS`,
`RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS=3`, `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=""`, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, the
`*_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME`s, the `EMAIL_*` block, `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED`). The genuine
differences:

### Backend (api + worker)

| Concern | Azure | AWS |
|---|---|---|
| Secret store | `SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault` + `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL` + `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` (the user-assigned identity must be *selected* — without it every Key Vault read fails) | `SECRET_STORE=aws_secrets_manager` + `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX` — no credential env at all; the task IAM role carries access |
| Token validation | Azure-native validator: `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_API_SCOPE`, `AZURE_ALLOW_GUEST_USERS` | Generic `OidcBearerScheme`: just `OIDC_ISSUER` + `OIDC_AUDIENCE`. The user profile resolves via the **userinfo endpoint**, because Cognito access tokens carry neither `email` nor `aud` |
| Secret injection | Container Apps secret refs | ECS `valueFrom` Secrets Manager ARNs — start-time snapshots, so a rotated infra secret needs a service bounce |
| Telemetry | `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318` (loopback into the ADOT sidecar) |
| Email | Any SMTP relay + tfvars-sourced addresses | SES SMTP host + an IAM-derived SMTP password secret + `alert_email` / `alert_email_to` variables |

### Frontend (runtime `DATAQ_*` contract — one nginx image, envsubst at startup)

Both set `DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM`, `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc`, `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY`,
`DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID`. The differences:

| | Azure | AWS |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | `DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE` (Entra wants the API scope requested) | `DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE="openid email profile"` |
| Sign-out | standard RP-initiated logout | `DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE=cognito` (Cognito's `/logout` wants `client_id` + `logout_uri`) |
| Origin guard | unset — open (Container Apps ingress is the only route in) | `DATAQ_ORIGIN_SECRET` (Secrets-Manager-injected; nginx 403s any request without the CloudFront-stamped header, `/_alb-health` exempt) |

For the local stack's configuration, see
[Running DataQ without Azure](deployment.md#running-dataq-without-azure) — the same seams,
pointed at compose services.

## Documentation
The comparison is now a permanent, published reference page: **[Deployment parity (Azure · AWS · Local)](https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/deployment-parity/)** ([docs/deployment-parity.md](docs/deployment-parity.md), merged as [#1383](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1383), Pages publish green and live-verified). It carries:

- the **hosting** table (compute, public surface, DB, queue, secret store, identity, observability, email, IaC — all three installations),
- the **features** table — including the **Assets / lineage / incidents / DQ scorecard row you flagged as missing**, now present (live-verified on Azure; same code deployed on AWS with the lineage sweep enabled but unexercised against that account's grants; Marquez profile locally),
- the **harness** table (Azure full / AWS none / local mirror),
- the `deploy.yml` vs `deploy-aws.yml` differences (login, tag namespace, migrate gating, roll-and-verify mechanism, in-workflow smoke, sidecar handling, the `ignore_changes` gotcha),
- the real config deltas read out of the two OpenTofu stacks — backend (secret store, token validation, secret injection, telemetry, email) and frontend `DATAQ_*` contract (scope, `LOGOUT_STYLE=cognito`, `DATAQ_ORIGIN_SECRET`).

It's linked from the Deployment page and sits in the Reference nav; `mkdocs build --strict` gated it, and the review came back clean.

## AWS rate-limit test — passed, and it settled the open question
This was the one unverified setting on the AWS stack (`RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS=3` behind CloudFront's extra hop). Live results against the CloudFront URL:

1. **Burst of 135 unauthenticated requests → exactly 120 × 401, then 15 × 429** — the per-IP cap enforced at precisely its configured 120/min, with `Retry-After: 21` and `X-Request-ID` on the 429 (the innermost-middleware behavior holding).
2. **Spoof resistance, the part a plain burst can't prove:** while limited, three requests with rotated client-spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` values all **stayed 429**. Spoofed entries only extend the chain leftward; with hops=3 the limiter selects the entry CloudFront itself appends (the real viewer IP), so a client cannot mint itself a fresh bucket — the depth is correct *and* unspoofable.
3. **Recovery:** the window reset cleanly to 401 after ~21 s — no lingering state.

The result is recorded on the parity page's rate-limiting row and in the project memory; the only remaining AWS-side asymmetry of any kind is SES sandbox mode, which needs an AWS support request rather than code.
